headline: GR SILVER SHATTERS OWN RECORD AT SAN MARCIAL: 45.1M AT 1,623 G/T AG INCLUDING 8.25M AT 8,579 G/T — PARALLEL BRECCIA TARGET ADDS NEW STRUCTURAL UPSIDE (TSXV:GRSL)
source_name: Investing News Network / GR Silver Mining Ltd.
snippet: GR Silver Mining (TSXV: GRSL) announced July 10 its best-ever drill result at the Plomosas Project in Sinaloa, Mexico: hole SMS26-04 at the San Marcial SE Extension returned 45.1 metres estimated true width at 1,623 g/t silver, including an 8.25-metre core at 8,579 g/t Ag — surpassing all previous intercepts in the project's history — while a second, newly discovered Parallel Breccia structure returned 6.15m at 447 g/t Ag in an adjacent hole, confirming the SE Extension boundary has expanded at least 150 metres beyond the 2023 NI 43-101 MRE. At $59+ silver and one of the highest-grade silver drill programs active in Mexico, the dual-discovery result in a single release changes the resource expansion trajectory at Plomosas from incremental to potentially step-change.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD 176,836 OZ IN Q2 AS GREENSTONE AND VALENTINE LIFT CANADIAN OUTPUT 11% QoQ — JULY 22 ORLA VOTE WILL CREATE NORTH AMERICA'S NO. 2 GOLD MINER (TSX:EQX)
snippet: Equinox Gold (TSX: EQX) reported July 9 that Q2 2026 gold production reached 176,836 ounces — with combined output from the Greenstone and Valentine mines in Canada rising 11% quarter-over-quarter as both flagship operations ramped toward steady-state — positioning the company to meet full-year guidance ahead of the July 22 special shareholder meeting to approve its all-share combination with Orla Mining, which will create a North America-focused gold producer with 1.1 million oz/yr combined output and a $18.5 billion combined market value. The Q2 production beat is the strongest possible argument in favour of the merger rationale: the assets behind the deal are delivering, not just projecting.

headline: G MINING TOCANTINZINHO GRADUATES: 36,845 OZ GOLD IN Q2, +16% QoQ — ON TRACK FOR 160,000–190,000 OZ FULL-YEAR FROM BRAZIL (TSX:GMIN)
snippet: G Mining Ventures (TSX: GMIN) reported July 9 that the Tocantinzinho Gold Mine in Pará State, Brazil delivered 36,845 ounces of gold in Q2 2026, a 16% increase over Q1, with the company reiterating full-year guidance of 160,000 to 190,000 ounces and confirming that Tocantinzinho is tracking to planned production rates as the mine exits its early-ramp phase. Tocantinzinho is one of the cleanest junior-to-producer graduation stories in the current gold cycle — a greenfield open-pit mine that entered commercial production in 2024 and is now consistently growing output quarter-over-quarter at $4,100/oz gold, generating operating cash flow sufficient to fund both sustaining capex and exploration without equity dilution.

headline: TOREX MEDIA LUNA PROCESSES 10,793 TPD — ABOVE DESIGN CAPACITY IN Q2 AS GRADES RAMP AND MEDIA LUNA NORTH FIRST ORE TARGETS Q4 2026 (TSX:TXG)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Torex Gold Resources Inc.
snippet: Torex Gold (TSX: TXG) reported Q2 2026 production of 96,297 oz AuEq at its ELG Underground and Media Luna operations in Mexico, with processing plant throughput averaging 10,793 tpd — above design capacity — while the company remained confident in its 420,000–470,000 oz AuEq full-year guidance as mined grades are scheduled to improve through Q3 and increase further in Q4; Media Luna North is on schedule to deliver its first ore before year-end 2026. Throughput exceeding design at a new underground mine in its first full year is the critical early indicator that infrastructure assumptions in the feasibility study are conservative rather than optimistic — and Media Luna North first ore before year-end creates an incremental production catalyst not yet baked into most models.

headline: JAGUAR MAPS 15KM PACIENCIA GOLD DISTRICT IN BRAZIL'S IRON QUADRANGLE — SANTA ISABEL MINE REOPEN TARGETED END 2026 AFTER DISTRICT-SCALE DRILLING (TSX:JAG)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Jaguar Mining Inc.
snippet: Jaguar Mining (TSX: JAG) announced July 8 that 3,764 metres of drilling in 17 holes along the Paciencia Trend in Minas Gerais, Brazil has connected the Chamé, Santa Isabel, Marzagão, and Bahú targets into a single corridor exceeding 15 kilometres of strike — including intercepts of 7.85m at 2.03 g/t Au and 5.8m at 3.43 g/t Au — while the company advances the Santa Isabel mine toward a potential reopening by end-2026 through dewatering, underground rehabilitation, and a new underground drill program ahead of a formal technical report. Defining a 15km multi-target gold district in the Iron Quadrangle — the same greenstone belt that hosts Vale's iron ore empire and dozens of operating gold mines — replaces the exploration risk of point discovery with the more defensible thesis of a district-scale mineral system with multiple reopenable historical mines.

headline: GSP RESOURCE COMMENCES FIRST MODERN DRILL TEST OF MER PORPHYRY COPPER TARGET, ADJACENT TO HIGHLAND VALLEY — BC'S BIGGEST CU DISTRICT (TSXV:GSPR)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / GSP Resource Corp.
snippet: GSP Resource (TSXV: GSPR) announced July 8 that Phase 1 drilling at the Alwin high-grade gold target in Highland Valley, British Columbia is complete with 1,150 metres across four holes now at the laboratory, and that the first modern drill test of the adjacent Mer porphyry copper target has commenced — an untested geophysical anomaly with surface rock samples up to 1.02% Cu and TerraSpec alteration signatures (paragonitic muscovite + magnesium-iron chlorite) consistent with a proximal porphyry environment. Mer sits immediately adjacent to Highland Valley Copper, Teck Resources' 40-year-old, 180,000 tonne/yr copper mine — and the proximity to a proven porphyry system, combined with gold Alwin providing a real-time funding backstop, makes this among the more logically placed small-cap copper exploration programs in Canada.

headline: MATSA STACKS MULTIPLE HIGH-GRADE GOLD ZONES BELOW 1.7KM FORTITUDE NORTH ANOMALY — OPEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT LAKE CAREY, WA (ASX:MAT)
snippet: Matsa Resources (ASX: MAT) reported July 10 that diamond drilling at the Fortitude North prospect within the Lake Carey Gold Project in Western Australia continues to confirm multiple stacked, high-grade gold zones beneath a previously identified 1.7-kilometre-long aircore gold anomaly, with the mineralised system remaining open in both along-strike directions — indicating current drilling has not yet defined the full extent of the gold system. Lake Carey's potential to host a district-scale gold corridor makes Fortitude North one of the more underappreciated drill programs on the ASX, given the property's position in the same Eastern Goldfields structural province that hosts several multi-million-ounce deposits at comparable project stages.

headline: RARE EARTHS AMERICAS IDENTIFIES GIANT REE-NIOBIUM CARBONATITE SYSTEM AT HOMER — 15,000M DRILL PROGRAM UNDERWAY IN BRAZIL'S GOIÁS ALKALINE PROVINCE
source_name: Yahoo Finance / Rare Earths Americas, Inc.
snippet: Rare Earths Americas announced approximately July 6 that exploration work at its 100%-owned Homer-A Project in Brazil's Goiás Alkaline Province — covering 1,233 km² of tenements — has identified a large rare earth-niobium alkaline-carbonatite system with three large magnetic anomalies corresponding to potential REE-Nb deposits, including a 17 km-wide ring structure at Homer A (~749 km² footprint), with a 15,000-metre drill program now underway and first results expected Q3 2026. The Goiás Alkaline Province hosts some of the world's most significant niobium deposits — including CBMM's Araxá mine, which accounts for 80% of global niobium supply — and a rare earth-niobium discovery within the same province's structural domain represents one of the few legitimate district-scale exploration opportunities in a critical mineral that China does not yet control.

headline: FIVE INSTITUTIONS AGREE: Q2 SELLOFF CHANGED THE ENTRY PRICE, NOT THE STRUCTURAL CASE FOR GOLD — STATE STREET TARGETS $4,750–$5,500 BY EARLY 2027 | GoldSilver.com
snippet: A GoldSilver.com digest of five concurrent institutional notes — State Street, Goldman Sachs, the World Gold Council, UBS, and MKS PAMP — finds unanimous agreement that the Q2 2026 gold selloff (from $5,300+ in January to $4,100 by July) represents a repricing of rate-sensitive Western demand rather than a fundamental shift in who is buying gold, with State Street targeting $4,750–$5,500 by early 2027, Goldman defending its $4,900 end-2026 target, and UBS projecting $5,200 over the next 12 months. The five-institution consensus is significant precisely because these houses disagree on almost everything else in fixed income and equities: when Goldman's commodity desk, UBS's CIO, the WGC, State Street Global Advisors, and MKS PAMP all independently reach the same conclusion about structural demand continuity, the burden of proof shifts to the bears.

headline: AURA 75,437 GEO FROM SIX MINES IN Q2 — BORBOREMA RAMP AND MSG ACQUISITION LIFT OUTPUT 18% ABOVE Q2 2025 (NASDAQ:AUGO)
snippet: Aura Minerals (NASDAQ: AUGO) reported July 10 preliminary Q2 2026 production of 75,437 gold equivalent ounces across its six operating mines — Aranzazu, Apoena, Minosa, Almas, Borborema, and newly acquired Mineração Serra Grande (MSG) — with year-over-year output 18% above Q2 2025 as both the Borborema mine (commercial production 2025) and MSG (acquired late 2025) added ounces not present in the prior year's base. Aura's six-mine portfolio across Brazil, Honduras, and Mexico represents a multi-jurisdiction, multi-asset gold producer structure that insulates against single-mine operational risk — a structure that historically commands a valuation premium in gold equity markets, though Aura currently trades at a discount to peer multiples that its YoY growth profile suggests is unwarranted.
